mission.title:
What we mean when we say
"the next century."

body.text: There is a kind of company that is good at being a company - at growing, optimising, returning capital. There is another kind of company that is good at the work. Both are needed; they are not the same thing.

Wesan is in the second category, by choice and by design. We are organised so that three different kinds of long-horizon work - software, interactive media, and eventually heavy industry - can each have a fair chance of being done well. Some of that work will not pay back inside a decade. Some of it might not pay back at all. We took that into account when we set the building up.
We chose the name Wesan - Old English, "to be" - because we wanted a verb that didn't promise anything specific. The name doesn't tell you what we make. It tells you we intend to stay.
Solo today, by design.

Wesan is one person right now. That is the design, not the limitation. Three products in build - Friday and Dante in beta, Notch in development - run by the same hand, on the same calendar, under the same standard. This is only possible because the tools have caught up: AI lets one engineer hold what used to need five. Wesan is built to take that leverage seriously - and to keep being honest about what it is the day before the second person joins, and the day after.
Friday is built with Friday. Dante is built with Friday. The compounding is real, and it is the whole reason this structure can begin with one person and still mean to last a century.

body.text: Three commitments.
One. Patient time. Every division gets the runway it needs to do the work - without quarterly pressure, without short-cycle metrics. The point is to remove fear from the engineering room.

Two. Real autonomy. The roof exists to protect the rooms, not to give them orders. Software ships when it's ready. Studio ships when the work is done. Industries waits as long as it has to. Each division sets its own roadmap, hires its own people, picks its own fights.
Three. Plain reporting. Once a year, in April, every division publishes what worked, what didn't, and what it spent. Not a marketing report. A field report.

We are not in a hurry, and we are not slow. We work on the timescale of the things we're building. If a thing should last a century, then the company that builds it should act like one. That is what we are trying to be.
- Can AKYUZ, FOUNDER · Belgium, MAY 2026

founder.name: Can Akyuz
founder.lead: Engineer by self-teaching, founder by need. I started Wesan because the work I wanted to do didn't fit cleanly in any of the rooms that already existed.
paragraphs: Background in mathematics - formal degree, then everything after that taught to myself. Five-plus years writing software across products and tools I needed. Wesan is the first thing I have started that I want to finish.
Building Wesan from London, with a focus on useful products and the engineering foundation behind them.

products.name: Meltir
products.tagline: One workspace for your working day
products.desc: An AI workspace in development, bringing calendar, email, tasks, voice and meeting notes into one assistant. Designed to connect context with practical actions while keeping the user in control.

products.name: Levios AI
products.desc: A social content assistant in development for cafes, salons, shops and other small businesses. Upload a photo and describe the result. Get brand-aware visual variations, captions and a content plan to review.

products.name: wesanjs
products.desc: A multi-tenant commerce platform in development, supporting storefronts, product data and business operations. It provides shared infrastructure for our commerce products.

products.name: Friday
products.desc: A daemon that runs your coding agents. Claude Code today, others tomorrow. Detach, attach, ship from anywhere - terminal, desktop, or phone. BYOM. In development, no public link yet.

products.name: Dante
products.desc: Tasks, workouts, nutrition, supplements, spending, habits - consolidated into one quiet surface. Turkish food + supplement database built in. Local-first. TestFlight now, App Store soon.

products.name: Notch
products.tagline: Habits, in the discipline of a daily log
products.desc: A habit tracker built for people who already keep a log somewhere. One screen, one tap, end-of-day review. No streaks-as-pressure, no notifications. Just the checkmark, done quietly.

products.name: Levios
products.desc: A system that turns a domain model into working admin and ops panels. Built on the wesanjs runtime with domain-driven design - define the domain once, generate the panels around it. In development.

principles: SHIP WHEN READY
No quarterly roadmap. A release ships the morning the work is done - sometimes that's next Tuesday, sometimes it's next year.
THE DIFF IS THE CONTRACT
Every change a user can see is something they can refuse. We don't silently rewrite preferences, accounts, or files.
SMALL TEAMS, LONG ROPES
Founder-led development today. Product scope, customer feedback and tested releases guide how we grow.

studio.manifesto: Wesan Studio makes games. Two are live on the App Store - Empire Inc., a business simulation, and Block Forge, a single-player puzzle - built by the same hand that builds everything else here. More ship when they're good, not before.

projects.name: Empire Inc.
projects.desc: A business-simulation game: build an empire from zero - master markets, compete globally, earn while you sleep. Live on the App Store.

projects.name: Block Forge
projects.desc: A single-player block puzzle: arrange blocks, climb the local leaderboard, unlock cosmetics with in-game currency. No account, no real-money purchases. Live on the App Store.

principles: NO QUARTERLY
We don't set release dates we don't believe in. The studio ships when the thing is done; nobody is ever the first to learn the date.
SMALL CREWS
Each project carries 4–8 people, end-to-end. The same hand that designs the world writes the dialogue and edits the trailer.
ART OVER PRESSURE
The studio is funded from the holding, not from the calendar. Nothing about the room is structured to reward looking busy.

studio01.title: A game about return.

photo.caption: A FICTIONAL ANATOLIAN COASTAL TOWN · THE YEAR AFTER A SMALL EARTHQUAKE
photo.label: REFERENCE · NOT FINAL

premise: A single-player game about return, set in a fictional Anatolian coastal town in the year after a small earthquake. You come home. The town is mostly still standing. The people are still here. The story is what you do with that fact.

We hope it takes about eight hours to play. We are giving it three years. The smaller scope is on purpose - this is the studio's first project, and we want to ship something we are proud of, on the timescale of a real human life.

answersHead.label: WORKING ANSWERS
answersHead.title: Where we are on the big questions.
answersHead.sub: Answers below will change. We will date this page as they do.

answers: Narrative adventure, in the lineage of Kentucky Route Zero, Disco Elysium, and the quieter parts of Outer Wilds.
Third-person, fixed camera, hand-painted environments. No combat. No fail states beyond the social.
PC and Mac on day one. Consoles in the year after release. No mobile, no cloud-streaming, no live-service hook.
Written in English and Turkish in parallel - not a localisation, a co-authoring. Other languages from the community after.
About eight hours, one playthrough. We will not pad it. We will not gate it. New game plus only if it actually adds something.
Premium, one-time, around $30. No DLC plans. We are not running a season.

studio02.title: Six shorts, ten minutes each. Watch once. Open it up.
premise: Six interactive shorts, ten minutes each. Documentary form, fictional subject. Built to be watched once and then opened up - every viewer follows a different thread the second time.

The format is film first, software second. You don't have to interact to watch it. But if you do, the camera turns. The interview shifts. The thread you missed appears in the margin. It is built for the web, not for a streaming service - it lives at its own URL and we hope it stays there.

shortsHead.label: THE SIX SHORTS
shortsHead.title: Working list, in working order.
shortsHead.sub: None of these titles are final. Three of them probably will not survive the year. That's the point of a working list.

shorts: A morning on the Bosphorus, with three people who take it every day, who don't know each other.
A pay phone in a village square in Edirne that still works, used now mostly by tourists.
The hour before bread rises. The pace, the silence, the radio.
Twelve hours with a Yemeksepeti driver, told in twelve cuts.
What a family has saved, what they have thrown out, in a hundred-year apartment.
A return. The shape of the city seen from the other side.
format: A linear ten-minute film. No menus, no choices, no UI. You can close the laptop and walk away. That is the work.
A second viewing reveals threads in the margin - a longer interview, a different cut, a photograph that wasn't in the film. You decide what to follow.
Every viewer who chooses the same path sees the same thing. We did not build a generative film. We built a film with side doors.
Each short releases free at its own URL, available to download as a single MP4 with subtitles. The interactive layer is optional, the file is the truth.
timeline: Director and cinematographer in. First short in pre-production.
Short 01 · THE FIRST FERRY - public release at its own URL.
Shorts 02–06, one every two months. Open release on the day each is finished.
A single archive page collecting all six. A small physical edition for festivals.

head.label: TRUST & SECURITY
head.title: Plain answers to the hard questions.
head.sub: Wesan is small and self-financed. We don't have a SOC 2 report yet, because no customer has needed one. When the first one does - and they will - we will get one. This page is where we'll publish it.

today: Hardware security keys (WebAuthn) required for every employee with access to production. No SMS, no TOTP. SSO via Workspace, with break-glass procedures documented and tested quarterly.
TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest. Customer data encrypted with per-tenant keys; key rotation is automated, ninety-day cycle, no manual touch.
No public SSH. Bastion-only access, audited. Production lives in eu-central-1 and eu-west-1 (AWS). No instance has both ingress and egress to the open internet.
Every production change is a reviewed pull request. We do not push directly to main. Deploy keys are short-lived (8 hours) and tied to a specific build artifact, not a human.
Sev-1 incidents are paged within five minutes; the founder is on the rotation. Post-incident reports are written within seven days, public for our own products, available under NDA for B2B.
Daily encrypted backups, retained 30 days. Quarterly restore tests, results published internally. We have never had to restore from backup in production. Yet.
gaps: Not started. We will engage an auditor the first time a B2B customer requires it. Estimated 6 months from start to Type I report.
Not started. Will follow SOC 2 by approximately 12 months if there is European enterprise demand.
Not applicable today. We don't handle PHI; if a product ever does, we will go through the full process and disclose here.
Not started. Will be required for any U.S. federal work in Industries. Multi-year process.
Not run. We accept disclosed vulnerabilities at security@wesan.co and respond within 5 business days. A formal bounty program will start in 2027.
Internal red-team quarterly. External pen-test scheduled annually starting Q3 2026.

head.label: LEGAL
head.title: The fine print. Plain language. No tricks.
head.sub: Wesan operates under Turkish company law. The documents below apply to wesan.co and all Wesan division websites. Each product (Friday, Dante, Notch) has its own additional terms; those live on the product's own site.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
body: In one sentence
We collect as little as possible, store it as briefly as possible, share it with as few people as possible.
What we collect
When you visit wesan.co we collect the standard request log (IP, user-agent, page visited, timestamp). We use this only to find bugs and detect abuse. Logs are kept 30 days, then deleted.
What we do not collect
No tracking pixels. No third-party analytics on this site. No cookies that survive the session. No advertising identifiers, ever.
When you write to us
Emails sent to press@, partner@, or hello@wesan.co are stored in our mail provider (Fastmail, in the EU). We keep correspondence for as long as we are talking; we delete threads on request.
When you apply for a job
Applications go to a separate tracker. We keep them for 12 months after the role closes, then delete. You can ask for deletion at any time at hello@wesan.co.
Your rights
If you are in the EU, EEA, UK, or Türkiye: you have the right to access, correct, export, or delete any data we hold about you. Write to hello@wesan.co - we reply within 14 days, usually faster.
Changes
We will date the top of this page when we change it. If the change is material, we will note it on the homepage for 30 days.

terms.title: Terms of use
body: In one sentence
Browse the site, share the writing, link to anything - just don't pretend to be us, and don't hammer the server.
What the site is
wesan.co is the marketing and information site for Wesan A.Ş. and its divisions. Nothing on this site is a contract, a financial offer, or a regulatory commitment.
What you can do
You can read, share, link, quote, and screenshot anything here. No need to ask. Attribution is appreciated.
What you can't do
Don't impersonate Wesan. Don't scrape the site to train a model without telling us. Don't use the trademarks on a product that isn't ours.
No warranties
The site is provided as-is. We don't promise it will be online every second; we do try.
Governing law
These terms are governed by Turkish law. Disputes go to the İstanbul Anatolian courts.

cookies.title: Cookies
body: How many cookies do we use?
Zero persistent ones. One session cookie if you actively interact with a form, deleted when you close the tab.
No banners
No cookie banner, because there is nothing that requires consent under EU or Turkish law. The session cookie is strictly necessary; that's the only kind we use.
No analytics
We don't use Google Analytics, Plausible, Fathom, or any third-party analytics on this site. We look at the server logs once a week. That's it.
When products use cookies
Friday, Dante, and Notch - when they have web surfaces - use their own cookies, documented on their own privacy pages.

trademark.title: Trademarks
body: Wesan™ and the W-mark
Wesan™ and the stylised W-mark are trademarks of Wesan, with registration pending in Türkiye, the EU, US, and Japan.
Product marks
Friday™, Dante™, and Notch™ are trademarks of Wesan A.Ş. They are not registered yet.
Fair use

You may use the Wesan name and W-mark to refer to our company - in articles, presentations, news. You may not modify them, combine them with another mark, or use them in a way that suggests endorsement.
Press kit
For official versions of the logos, see the press kit at /press.
Questions
If you're not sure whether your use is OK, write to hello@wesan.co. We will reply yes or no, in writing, within a week.

dpa.title: Data Processing Agreement · for business customers
body: When this applies
Only when you (a business) use a Wesan product in a way that has Wesan acting as a data processor for personal data you control. For most uses, this does not apply.
Standard contractual clauses
We sign the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (2021/914) and the UK addendum if your jurisdiction requires it. We do not use binding corporate rules.
Sub-processors
A current list of sub-processors is published at /legal/subprocessors, with at least 30 days' notice before changes. As of May 2026: AWS (eu-central-1, eu-west-1), Fastmail, Stripe.
Security

Encryption at rest and in transit. Hardware security keys mandatory for employees with production access. We will publish our security overview at /trust when the first enterprise customer asks for it.
How to sign
Email partner@wesan.co with your legal entity's name. We send a counter-signed copy within 48 hours.

head.label: INVESTORS · CAPITAL STRUCTURE
head.title: There are no outside investors. There are no plans to raise.
head.sub: This page exists because we are asked, often, who funds Wesan. The answer is short: Wesan funds itself. The longer answer is below.

structure: Wesan is privately held by its founder. The Software division generates operating cash; that cash is the only source of capital for the company. We do not draw bank lines, we do not have a venture round, and we have not taken any outside equity.

Long-horizon work needs runway, not a board meeting. Every division gets a minimum 10-year runway from the holding before any expectation of returning capital. That guarantee is meaningless if a third party can revoke it at the next valuation milestone.

In principle, never. In practice - if a sovereign or foundation came forward with capital that matched our timescale and accepted our governance, we would consider it. We have not had that conversation with anyone.
investors.capTableFooter: * No formal entity registration yet - Wesan is in formation. Employee equity will be designed when the first hire comes in; no pool exists today.

principlesHead.label: FINANCIAL PRINCIPLES
principlesHead.title: What we do with the money we make.

principles: ONE
A division's operating cash funds that division's runway. Software's margin is Software's to spend.
TWO
A division does not subsidise another division indefinitely. Studio and Industries have explicit budgets from the holding, with explicit timelines for being self-sustaining.
THREE
No dividends. Profits are reinvested into the next division until the company itself is a hundred years older.
FOUR
No share buybacks. Wesan does not have public shares to buy back, and will not create them.
FIVE
No leverage at the holding level. Each division may take on operational debt; the roof carries none.
faq: Yes. The structure was set up to make raising hard, on purpose.
Could we acquire one of the divisions?
No. Divisions are not for sale, and the structure does not allow a division to be spun out under outside ownership.
Is the founder open to a side conversation?
No. Every signal would have to come through partner@wesan.co, in writing, and it would be declined. We say this so nobody has to interpret silence.
Not in the next twenty years. After that, we will see what the next person at the helm thinks.
Could a sovereign or foundation fund Industries?
Only with governance that matched our existing structure - non-controlling, non-voting, non-redeemable. We have not had that conversation.

body.content: Friday is in early beta starting today. Daemon-first architecture, Rust core, Tauri + SolidJS desktop, Expo mobile companion. Wraps the Claude Code CLI as the primary agent runtime, with more backends planned.
What it is

A pair-programmer that lives in the terminal you already have open. It plans the task, edits the files, runs the tests, and shows you a reviewable diff at the end. The loop ends when the work is done - not when the model runs out of patience.
Why daemon-first

Because the agent loop needs to outlive the editor tab. Friday runs as a background daemon (Rust + tokio + gRPC), with thin clients on desktop, mobile, and CLI. You can detach, walk away, reattach hours later, and the work is where you left it.
How to try

products.name: Meltir
products.title: One workspace for your working day

body.text: An AI workspace in development, bringing calendar, email, tasks, voice and meeting notes into one assistant. Designed to connect context with practical actions while keeping the user in control.
Context in one place.
Meltir is designed to connect conversations with calendar, mail, tasks and meeting notes. Planned voice and live transcription features help capture information without switching between tools.
Assistance that leads to action.

We are developing model integrations and connected workflows for summarising context, preparing drafts and organising work. Product availability and integration coverage will be announced as they are tested.

A social content assistant in development for cafes, salons, shops and other small businesses. Upload a photo and describe the result. Get brand-aware visual variations, captions and a content plan to review.
From a photo to a post.

Send a photo and a short message, typed or spoken. The planned workflow applies your brand and product profiles, suggests two to four visual variations and a caption, and lets you choose or request a change. A simple editor handles text, cropping and size.
A week of content, reviewed by you.

The planned batch workflow turns 10 to 20 photos into a weekly or monthly content calendar. You review each item before it is published. A short brand setup captures your logo, colours, tone, sector and example posts so you do not need to write a detailed prompt each time.
Built for small businesses.

Our initial audience is businesses with one to ten people: cafes, restaurants, salons, boutiques, furniture shops, florists and estate agents. We are starting with customer discovery in Turkey and London.
Publishing is part of the roadmap.

We plan scheduling and publishing for Instagram, Facebook and TikTok, subject to platform permissions and review. Direct publishing and handoff to the social app are separate paths. Music and native stickers depend on the platform and cannot be promised for every format. Video generation, team approvals and advanced analytics are later work.
A multi-tenant commerce platform in development, supporting storefronts, product data and business operations. It provides shared infrastructure for our commerce products.

products.name: Friday
products.title:
An agent runtime,
not another agent.

body.text: Everyone is shipping an agent. Friday is the thing the agents run inside.

Friday is a daemon for your coding agents. It runs Claude Code today and whatever comes next tomorrow - start a session in the terminal, detach, and re-attach from your desktop or your phone. Bring your own model; the runtime is free during the beta.
Built on the Agent Client Protocol.

Friday speaks ACP - the Agent Client Protocol, the open standard Zed released in August 2025 to do for coding agents what the Language Server Protocol did for language servers: one JSON-RPC interface between the thing that drives the agent (the client - an editor, a terminal, a phone) and the agent itself.

Before ACP, every editor-and-agent pairing was custom work - N editors times M agents, each integration hand-built, each agent locked to the handful of clients it bothered to support. ACP collapses that to N + M: any ACP client can drive any ACP agent, with no lock-in.

Friday sits on the agent side of that line. It hosts your agents as long-lived sessions and exposes them over ACP - locally as a subprocess speaking JSON-RPC over stdio, and remotely over HTTP and WebSocket. The editor on your laptop and the companion in your pocket are just two ACP clients talking to the same session.
ACP gives the agent an editor. MCP gives it tools.

They are complementary, not competing. MCP is how an agent reaches tools and data; ACP is how an agent reaches a human and a workspace - diffs to approve, files to read, permissions to grant. Friday reuses MCP's JSON shapes where it can and adds the editor-facing types ACP defines. You keep your MCP tools; Friday owns the client side.
Detach. Attach. Ship from anywhere.

An agent is just a process, and processes need somewhere to live - to start, persist, recover, and be reached. That somewhere is Friday. Close the laptop and the run keeps going; open your phone on the train and you are in the same session, watching the same diff land.
Friday is built with Friday. The compounding is the whole point - and the reason a runtime, not another agent, is what was missing.
The agent is the easy part. The runtime - the thing that keeps it alive and lets you reach it from anywhere - is the product.
- WESAN SOFTWARE · Belgium
You don't need six apps to run one day.
Dante folds tasks, workouts, nutrition, supplements, spending, and habits into one quiet surface - opened once a day, holding the basics without asking for your attention.
Local-first, not cloud-rented.

Your day lives on your device, not on someone's server. Dante is built local-first: every entry is written to a local store first, the app works fully offline, and sync - when it exists - is an enhancement, never a requirement. Nothing to sign up for before you start, and nothing leaves the phone unless you decide it should.

The bet is simple. The most personal data you keep - what you ate, what you spent, what you lifted - should not be the price of using a tracker. Local-first means the data is yours by architecture, not by privacy policy.
The Turkish gap.

Every nutrition tracker assumes an American pantry. Dante ships with a Turkish food and supplement database built in - the foods people here actually eat, the brands on the actual shelf - so logging a meal isn't a custom entry every single time.
Consolidation, not features.
Every tracker you install is another notification, another login, another thing to forget. Dante's bet is the opposite: one place, six trackers, no noise. On TestFlight now; App Store soon.
The best tracker is the one you actually open - and the one whose data never leaves your hands.
- WESAN SOFTWARE · Belgium

products.name: Notch
products.title:
Habits, in the discipline
of a daily log.

body.text: A habit tracker for people who already keep a log.
One screen, one tap, an end-of-day review. No streak counter, no badges, no 9pm push. Notch is for people who don't need to be nagged into their habits - only to be counted.
Against the streak.

Most habit apps run on manufactured guilt: the unbroken streak you're afraid to lose, the red day, the notification engineered to pull you back. It works for a while, and then the streak breaks and you delete the app - because the app was never about the habit, it was about the streak.

Notch removes the whole apparatus. No extrinsic pressure, because pressure borrows motivation it can't pay back. What's left is the habit and a record of it. The motivation has to be yours; Notch just keeps the count honest.
The log is the reward.

Notch treats your habits the way a journal treats your days: an append-only log, one entry at a time, reviewed once at the end of the day. Nothing to optimise, no number to protect - only the quiet satisfaction of a checkmark and a record that's true. The log is the point.
Discipline doesn't need a notification. The log is the reward.
- WESAN SOFTWARE · Belgium
Define the domain once. Get the panels.
Levios turns a domain model into working admin and ops panels - the internal tools you'd otherwise hand-build, generated from the model that already describes your business.
The domain is the single source.

Most internal tools get assembled twice: once as a domain model in the codebase, and again as the screens that read and edit it. The two drift. A field changes in the model; three panels forget. Levios collapses them - the domain model is the single source, and every panel is derived from it. Change the model, the panels follow.
Domain-Driven Design, made executable.

Levios takes DDD literally. Entities, value objects, aggregates, and the invariants between them aren't documentation - they're the input. Levios reads the domain's structure and its rules and emits panels that already respect them: the right fields, the right validation, the right relationships, the right boundaries between aggregates.
Built on wesanjs.

Underneath is wesanjs - the runtime the rest of Wesan is built on. Levios is the layer that turns a wesanjs domain into a usable surface, so a new internal panel is a description, not a project. It is the tool that builds Wesan's own tools.
Stop hand-building the same admin panel. Describe the domain; let the panels follow.
- WESAN SOFTWARE · Belgium
